They are structured to the layouts that ICH, EMA and FDA expect and are aligned with those expectations. They are not a regulatory assessment and are not a substitute for any study those frameworks require. No value in the document is a dose recommendation. The platform is a beta release. Version strings are printed in every output and results can be compared only with results produced under the same versions. Files in this record are restricted; access may be requested from the record page.
items.title: mosaeQ Regulatory Rehearsal — User Guide and Knowledge Document, v1.3-beta

items.summary: High interpolation accuracy does not establish that physical parameters are identifiable. We study this distinction in a controlled Kiselev black hole benchmark with a validated timelike-emitter and three-dimensional null-geodesic shooting calculation. The exact $k=0$ boundary provides an analytically known null control because the spacetime becomes Schwarzschild and independent of $w_q$. Ringdown is informative for the deformation amplitude $k$, while photon geometry supplies an independent response direction that resolves much of the $w_q$ degeneracy. Relative to ringdown alone, ringdown plus photon geometry gives a median pointwise $4.54\times$ gain in minimum singular value and a $2.28\times$ improvement in Jacobian condition number. In grouped physical interpolation, identifiable-$w_q$ normalized mean absolute error decreases from 0.309 to 0.087. Random splitting is more optimistic, while directional extrapolation is substantially harder and split-conformal coverage degrades under distribution shift. A non-learned nearest-model inverse shows that the gain is not confined to the tested learned architectures. A uniform 161-phase audit gives a typical normalized prediction shift of $9.48\times10^{-4}$, while a targeted 321-phase audit resolves the remaining forward-feature comparisons. However, frozen HGB and random-forest tail shifts exceed prespecified robustness thresholds. Thus, physical observable complementarity is supported, but inverse-estimator robustness remains conditional. This is a theoretical identifiability benchmark, not an observational constraint.
items.title: Learning When Black Hole Hair Is Observable: Physical Identifiability, Generalization, and Observable Complementarity

items.summary: Agentic memory allows LLM agents to reuse past experience, yet retrieved memories can also distort inference even when they are benign, correctly stored, and appropriately retrieved. We study this failure mode, which we call memory over-reliance. Across benchmarks and memory architectures, we find that memory is useful when past experience transfers to the current task, but can become misleading when only part of the evidence transfers. Failures are strongest under partial query-memory overlap, a pattern further confirmed by controlled experiments thatvary the amount of overlapping evidence. Motivated by this finding, we propose MEMTRIM, a plug-and-play framework that indexes memory evidence at write time and controls its reuse at read time. MEMTRIM removes repeated or conflicting evidence while preserving useful memory-specific information, requires no retraining, and applies to both embedding-based and structured memory systems.Experiments show that MEMTRIM reduces memory overreliance while preserving the benefits of useful memory across models and memory settings.
items.title: Understanding and Mitigating Inference-Time Overreliance Using Agentic Memory

items.summary: This repository contains five human-labeled benchmark datasets developed for the study 'Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models' . The datasets support evaluation of automated methods for literature screening, structured information extraction in knowledge synthesis, and scientific data discovery. The repository includes: Literature screening — machine learning in concrete materials science: 440 publications, including 272 labeled relevant and 168 labeled irrelevant. literature_screening_human_labels_ml_in_concrete.csv Literature screening — nanopore transport using molecular dynamics simulations: 205 publications, including 40 labeled relevant and 165 labeled irrelevant. literature_screening_human_labels_nanopore_transport.csv Literature screening — lithium extraction using NASICON-type materials: 200 publications, including 15 labeled relevant and 185 labeled irrelevant. literature_screening_human_labels_lithium_extraction.csv Knowledge synthesis — machine learning in concrete materials science: human labels for 50 full-text publications across five structured information fields: machine learning task, algorithm, binder system, prediction target, and input feature. knowledge_synthesis_extraction_human_labels_ml_in_concrete.csv Data discovery — silicate glass density: 200 publications, including 89 labeled as containing the target data and 111 labeled as not containing the target data. Supporting evidence for glass composition and density is also provided. data_discovery_human_labels_silicate_glass_density.csv The literature screening benchmark datasets provide DOI, publication year, title, abstract, and human relevance label. A label of  TRUE indicates that a publication was judged relevant according to the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria, whereas FALSE indicates that it was judged not relevant. The data discovery dataset uses the same binary labeling convention to indicate whether a publication contains the specified silicate glass density data. For the knowledge synthesis dataset, human annotations were assigned to five structured information fields using predefined controlled vocabularies. Details of benchmark construction, inclusion and exclusion criteria, annotation procedures, and inter-annotator agreement are provided in the Supplementary Information of the associated study.   Citation If you use these datasets, please cite both the associated publication and this repository: Li, Z., He, Q., Chen, W., Yang, K., & Gong, K. (2026). Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models [Preprint]. alphaXiv. https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.automating-literature-screening-llms Li, Z., He, Q., Chen, W., Yang, K., & Gong, K. (2026).  Human-labeled benchmarks for automated literature screening and knowledge synthesis [Dataset]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21853689
items.title: Human-labeled benchmarks for automated literature screening and knowledge synthesis
